description: Consumer banking assistant with transaction search and payment history tools.

tools.name: search_transactions
tools.description: Search the user's card and bank transactions. Returns transactions whose timestamp falls in [start_utc, end_utc). Both bounds are required and must be UTC ISO 8601 strings (e.g. 2026-07-01T04:00:00Z); start is inclusive, end is exclusive.

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text merchant or category filter (optional; empty returns all transactions in range)

tools.name: get_last_rent_payment
tools.description: Return the most recent rent payment on record for the user's account.

tools.name: get_recent_charges
tools.description: Return the user's most recent card charges (newest first). No filtering.

scenarios.title: starbucks-last-week
scenarios.user: How many times did I buy Starbucks last week?

checks.note: Starbucks rows Tue Jul 14 .. Fri Jul 17; the Jul 8 row is outside any 'last week' reading

scenarios.rationale: Now = WEDNESDAY Jul 22 2026, 8:15am EDT (UTC-4) — midweek on purpose so both week conventions agree on the interior. Bare 'last week' admits Sunday-start (en-US CLDR): Sun Jul 12..Sun Jul 19 = [2026-07-12T04:00Z, 2026-07-19T04:00Z), and Monday-start (ISO): Mon Jul 13..Mon Jul 20 = [2026-07-13T04:00Z, 2026-07-20T04:00Z). Four Starbucks rows (Tue Jul 14 .. Fri Jul 17 local) fall inside BOTH readings; the Jul 8 Starbucks row and the Whole Foods row must not be counted. No rows on the disputed edge days (Sun Jul 12, Sun Jul 19) so the correct count is convention-independent.

scenarios.title: rent-last-month-which-day
scenarios.user: Did I pay my rent last month? Which day?

checks.note: Paid 9:30pm EDT June 1; UTC timestamp reads June 2 — must answer June 1

scenarios.rationale: Now = Jul 26 2026 EDT, so 'last month' = June 2026 civil month in the user's zone: Jun 1 00:00 ET..Jul 1 00:00 ET = [2026-06-01T04:00Z, 2026-07-01T04:00Z) (EDT is UTC-4 throughout). The June rent row is timestamped 2026-06-02T01:30Z = Jun 1, 9:30pm EDT: the answer day is June 1 (UTC day June 2 is the trap). The Jul 2 row is this month's rent and must not be reported; a naive UTC June window still contains the right row, so the arg grading (exact civil-month bounds) carries the nl2time signal.

scenarios.title: gas-this-month-so-far
scenarios.user: How many times have I bought gas this month?

checks.note: Three July gas rows; the Jun 28 row is out of range

scenarios.rationale: 'This month' anchored at now = Jul 26 2026 8:15am EDT. Start is the civil month start: Jul 1 00:00 ET = 2026-07-01T04:00Z. The end of an in-progress period admits three defensible readings: now itself (2026-07-26T12:15Z), end of today (Jul 27 00:00 ET = 04:00Z), or end of the month (Aug 1 00:00 ET = 2026-08-01T04:00Z). Transactions cannot postdate now, so all three yield the same result set: gas on Jul 3, 12, 21 (count 3); Jun 28 excluded.

scenarios.title: purchases-yesterday-cross-midnight
scenarios.user: Did I make any purchases yesterday? What were they?

checks.note: Only the In-N-Out row is local-Friday
Must name the Friday-night purchase, not the UTC-day decoys

scenarios.rationale: Now = Saturday Jul 25 2026, 9:00am PDT (UTC-7). Yesterday = civil Friday Jul 24 in LA: [Jul 24 00:00 PT, Jul 25 00:00 PT) = [2026-07-24T07:00Z, 2026-07-25T07:00Z). Double trap: the In-N-Out row (2026-07-25T05:30Z) is Friday 10:30pm PDT — inside — while the Chevron row (2026-07-24T05:00Z) is Thursday 10:00pm PDT — outside — yet naive UTC-day bounds [Jul 24 00Z, Jul 25 00Z) select exactly the wrong one. Correct answer: one purchase, In-N-Out.

scenarios.title: between-explicit-dates-inclusive
scenarios.user: How many subscription charges hit my card between July 4th and July 10th?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: nl2time resolves the 'between' end day exclusive ([Jul 4, Jul 10)); the benchmark encodes the inclusive conversational reading ([Jul 4, Jul 11)) — nl2time issue filed

checks.note: Netflix Jul 4, Spotify Jul 7, NYTimes Jul 10 (3:05pm ET — lost if the end bound excludes July 10)

scenarios.rationale: 'Between July 4th and July 10th' is inclusive of both named days (ordinary conversational reading): [Jul 4 00:00 ET, Jul 11 00:00 ET) = [2026-07-04T04:00Z, 2026-07-11T04:00Z). The NYTimes row at 2026-07-10T19:05Z = Jul 10 3:05pm ET punishes an exclusive end (Jul 10 00:00 ET): that reading returns 2, not 3. The iCloud row on Jul 12 is outside. Count = 3.

scenarios.title: rent-payment-utc-day-rollback
scenarios.user: When did I last pay my rent?

checks.note: If a time is given it must be 10:05 pm local, not 2:05

scenarios.rationale: Pure time→NL: the tool takes no arguments and returns timestamp 2026-07-01T02:05Z. In America/New_York (EDT, UTC-4) that is Tuesday June 30, 10:05pm. Correct answers reference June 30; 'July 1' is the naive UTC reading and fails. clockTime only fires if the response includes a clock time (then it must be the local one).

scenarios.title: london-last-week-bst-bounds
scenarios.user: How many card payments did I make last week?

checks.note: Tue Jul 14 .. Fri Jul 17 rows; Jul 7 is the week before

scenarios.rationale: Now = WEDNESDAY Jul 22 2026, 1:15pm BST (UTC+1) — midweek so both week conventions agree on the interior. en-GB weeks start Monday: last week = Mon Jul 13 00:00 BST..Mon Jul 20 00:00 BST = [2026-07-12T23:00Z, 2026-07-19T23:00Z); the Sunday-start reading Sun Jul 12..Sun Jul 19 = [2026-07-11T23:00Z, 2026-07-18T23:00Z) is also admitted for the bare phrase. The BST trap: bounds land at 23:00Z, not midnight UTC. The four rows Tue Jul 14 .. Fri Jul 17 local fall inside both readings; no rows on the disputed edge days (Sun Jul 12, Sun Jul 19) or in the 23:00Z slivers, so the count is 4 under any admissible reading.

scenarios.title: on-the-fourth-of-july
scenarios.user: How many purchases did I make on the 4th of July?

checks.note: Party City (11:30am ET) + fireworks (10:45pm ET); Kroger was July 3, 9pm ET

scenarios.rationale: July 4 2026 (a Saturday) as a civil day in New York: [Jul 4 00:00 ET, Jul 5 00:00 ET) = [2026-07-04T04:00Z, 2026-07-05T04:00Z). The fireworks row (2026-07-05T02:45Z = Jul 4 10:45pm EDT) is inside; the Kroger row (2026-07-04T01:00Z = Jul 3 9:00pm EDT) is outside despite its UTC-day reading July 4. Naive UTC-day bounds count Kroger and drop the fireworks — count 2 only falls out of correct local bounds.

scenarios.title: since-explicit-date-open-end
scenarios.user: How many times have I eaten at Chipotle since June 15th?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: nl2time parses only 'June 15th' (a single day) — the 'since' open-range connector is unsupported; nl2time issue filed

checks.note: Jun 16, Jul 2, Jul 19; Jun 13 predates the start

scenarios.rationale: 'Since June 15th' = start at Jun 15 00:00 ET = 2026-06-15T04:00Z (EDT, UTC-4). Open-ended present admits end = now (2026-07-26T12:15Z) or end of today (Jul 27 00:00 ET = 04:00Z); rows cannot postdate now so both agree. Rows in range: Jun 16, Jul 2, Jul 19 (7:40pm EDT) → 3. The Jun 13 row is before the start.

scenarios.title: last-amazon-charge-weekend-or-not
scenarios.user: Was my most recent Amazon charge on a weekend?

checks.note: Friday evening is not a weekend

scenarios.rationale: Pure time→NL. Most recent Amazon charge = 2026-07-24T23:50Z = Friday Jul 24, 7:50pm EDT — a weekday, so the answer is no. Distractors: the newer Best Buy charge is Saturday (wrong merchant), and the UTC timestamp is 11:50pm Friday — same weekday, so this scenario grades weekday reasoning without a UTC trap (traps live elsewhere; not every case may be adversarial).
